summary: Adds a cross-order check, loom intake check, that proves a hand-split feature's slices together cover the spec they split: an order's frontmatter gains an optional slice block (of, spec, digest, manifest, covers), and when several orders in a checked directory share one slice.of, CheckSlices verifies every criterion level the spec declares is covered by exactly one slice, that all slices agree on a manifest digest matching the manifest's own file hashes, and that depends-on edges among them form no cycle and name no missing order. The implementation (salvaged from commit 432f912, already applied and staged in this worktree) is essentially complete and matches every acceptance criterion by direct read-through; this analysis verifies that claim file-by-file and identifies two untested branches plus a scope-lock conflict for the developer/QA stages to close before this ships.

acceptanceCriteria.statement: An order's frontmatter MUST accept an optional slice block (of, spec, digest, manifest, covers); an order with no slice block MUST validate exactly as it did before the field existed.
examples: internal/intake/order.go: Order.Slice *Slice, yaml tag "slice"; nil when absent
TestParseLeavesSliceNilWhenAbsent and TestParseReadsAnOptionalSliceBlock in internal/intake/parse_test.go prove both halves

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A spec criterion with observableVia api or ui MUST have one level to cover, and both MUST give it two (api and ui); AC1:ui covers only that level, a bare AC2 covers every level AC2 has.
examples: internal/intake/slice.go: levelsOf() and parseCoversEntry()
TestLevelsOf and TestParseCoversEntry in internal/intake/slice_test.go

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Across every order sharing one slice.of, loom intake check MUST report a violation naming the criterion and level for an uncovered level, for a level two slices both cover (naming both orders), and for a covers entry naming a criterion or level the spec does not have.
examples: internal/intake/slice_check.go: checkCoverage, checkLevelCoverage, applyCoversEntry
TestCheckSlicesReportsEachViolationKind cases: "uncovered level", "doubly covered level", "unknown covers criterion", "unknown covers level"

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Slices of one spec MUST report a violation when their slice.digest values differ, when a digest does not match the SHA-256 of its manifest file, or when a manifest-listed file no longer matches its recorded hash, naming the file.
examples: internal/intake/slice_check.go: checkDigestAgreement, checkManifestDigests, checkManifestFiles/checkListedFile
TestCheckSlicesReportsEachViolationKind cases: "slice.digest disagreement", "slice.digest does not match the manifest", "manifest-listed file hash mismatch"

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Slices of one spec MUST report a violation for a depends-on cycle among them, naming every order in the cycle, and for a depends-on entry naming no order in the directory.
examples: internal/intake/slice_check.go: checkDependsOnCycle (DFS via findCycle), checkDanglingDependsOn
TestCheckSlicesReportsEachViolationKind cases: "depends-on cycle", "dangling depends-on"

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A spec or manifest file that cannot be read MUST be a violation on the order naming it, and a path that leaves the project root MUST be a violation; an unverified split must never be reported valid.
examples: internal/intake/slice.go: isWithinProjectRoot, readRooted (lexical check, never calls FileReader on an escaping path)
TestCheckSlicesReportsEachViolationKind cases: "unreadable spec file", "unreadable manifest file", "slice.spec path leaves the project root", "slice.manifest path leaves the project root"

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A passing split MUST print one line per spec with its slice and level counts, and the exit code contract MUST stay unchanged: 0 only when every order is valid.
examples: cmd/loom/cmd/intake.go: checkIntakeSlices prints "%s: %d slice(s), %d level(s) covered"; summarizeIntakeCheck folds slicedSpecs()-len(summaries) into the existing invalid counter
TestIntakeCheckVerifiesASliceSplitEndToEnd, TestIntakeCheckFailsOnASliceCoverageGap in cmd/loom/cmd/intake_test.go

acceptanceCriteria.statement: templates/claude-feature-team/intake/TEMPLATE.md and README.md MUST document the slice block, and the existing template vocabulary test MUST still pass.
examples: TEMPLATE.md gains a commented slice: block plus a "SLICE" explanation section; README.md gains five bullet points describing the cross-order check
internal/intake/vocabulary_test.go is unmodified by the patch — checks only the pre-existing order-level fields, so it stays a regression guard, not new-behavior evidence

acceptanceCriteria.statement: A fixture modeled on the reagent-map split MUST pass (AC1 and AC3 covered once at each level by different slices, AC14 covered bare by one slice), and each violation above MUST have a test built by breaking that fixture in one way, which fails when the check is removed.
examples: internal/intake/slice_test.go: validReagentMapFixture() + TestCheckSlicesAcceptsTheReagentMapSplit
internal/intake/slice_check_test.go: TestCheckSlicesReportsEachViolationKind (13 break-one-thing cases) and TestCheckSlicesReportsEveryBrokenSpecIndependently

acceptanceCriteria.statement: Every new or changed function MUST have cyclomatic complexity below 7, every changed line MUST be covered by a test that can fail, and no file outside scope.paths MUST change except this run's own delivery record under docs/features/intake-slice-check/.
examples: git diff --stat confirms only internal/intake/**, cmd/loom/cmd/intake*.go, and templates/claude-feature-team/intake/** changed — all inside scope.paths

dataModelChanges.description: Order's YAML frontmatter gains an optional slice block (of, spec, digest, manifest, covers). An order with no block has Slice == nil and parses/validates exactly as before — additive and backward compatible under intake schema version 1.

architecturalFlags: This feature's own "Domain Language" section defines two new business concepts, Slice and Level, which the analyst's standing instruction would normally require adding to shared/DOMAIN_DICTIONARY.md. AC10 locks file changes to scope.paths (internal/intake/**, cmd/loom/cmd/intake*.go, templates/claude-feature-team/intake/**, docs/features/intake-slice-check/**), and DOMAIN_DICTIONARY.md is outside that set — so this analysis deliberately does not touch it. Flag for a human: either widen scope.paths in a follow-up order to add the two dictionary terms, or accept the gap for now.

internal/intake/validate.go performs no per-file validation of slice field formats (non-empty Of/Spec/Manifest, a well-formed Digest prefix); correctness is enforced only cross-order, inside CheckSlices, when a slice.of group of two or more exists. This matches the spec's own framing ("Today intake.Check validates one file at a time, so this adds the first check across orders") and is not a defect — noting it so a future reader doesn't mistake it for an oversight.

edgeCases.case: An order declares slice.of but shares it with no other order in the batch (a group of exactly one).
edgeCases.handling: CheckSlices still evaluates it as a group of one; every level its own covers list omits is reported uncovered, so a solo slice can never silently pass as a complete split. Proven by TestCheckSlicesEvaluatesAGroupOfOneSlice.

edgeCases.case: A covers entry's level suffix is syntactically present but not api or ui (e.g. AC1:mobile).
edgeCases.handling: applyCoversEntry rejects it before even looking up the criterion, with 'is not a level (api or ui)' (slice_check.go:351). Untested today — see developer tasks.

edgeCases.case: A manifest lists a file that no longer exists at all, rather than one whose content changed.
edgeCases.handling: checkListedFile reports '%s lists %q, which could not be read: %v' (slice_check.go:238), distinct from the hash-mismatch message. Untested today — see developer tasks.

edgeCases.case: Two slice.of groups appear in one batch, and only one of them is broken.
edgeCases.handling: CheckSlices evaluates each group independently and keeps collecting violations across groups rather than stopping at the first broken one. Proven by TestCheckSlicesReportsEveryBrokenSpecIndependently.

edgeCases.case: A spec package's criterion has no observableVia, or one outside {api, ui, both}.
edgeCases.handling: levelsOf returns ok=false; checkCoverage reports a violation naming the criterion against the spec file itself — the resolved Open Question's stated assumption, implemented exactly as written.

edgeCases.case: A depends-on cycle spans more than two orders within one slice.of group.
edgeCases.handling: findCycle's local DFS detects a cycle of any length and names every order on the cycle path, not just the two endpoints.
